slides.title: Meet Dot
slides.text: Dot the fox is a data detective. Dot solves cases with facts, not guesses.

slides.title: Data is facts in rows
slides.text: A table holds facts in rows and columns. A table full of facts does not answer anything yet. You have to make the answer show.

slides.title: Sort or group
slides.text: Sorting puts the rows in order, like smallest to biggest. Grouping puts rows of the same kind together and counts them.

slides.title: Who was in the lunchroom last?
slides.text: Sort by the column the question asks about. The question says last, so sort by time.

slides.title: Show me first
slides.text: Dot has one rule: you can only pin a claim when the view on the screen shows it. Most of each kind? Group and count.

words.means: facts, like names, times and numbers
put rows in order by one column
put the same kinds together and count them

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at Sort & Group and solve 4 cases. For each one ask: which column is the question about?
